feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Evidence: iterations 9 and 10 (wheel_radius 0.044 m) are the best and repeatable (52.1441), with s-bend progress 0.1604 and max_error 0.0617, slalom progress 0.110 and max_error 0.0676, and oval progress 0.110 and max_error 0.062. Iteration 8 (0.04 m) gave a smaller gain with s-bend max_error 0.0684. Iterations 6 and 7 showed that mass 0.5 kg and wheel_track 0.14 m lower progress, and iterations 0 to 4 showed that sensor span, footprint, lead and controller gains barely move max_error. So the Integrator has kept the controller unchanged. Interpret the race as follows. If the slalom max_error stays at or below 0.069 and progress holds, the geometry is confirmed for the final track. If max_error exceeds 0.069 on any development track, the drift margin is gone, and the fallback is wheel_radius 0.04 m. If noise_robustness is low, the unseen track may push the robot off the line, which also favours the 0.04 m fallback.
requested_changes: If every development track keeps max_error at or below 0.069 with progress at or above iteration 9 values (s-bend 0.1604, slalom 0.110), keep wheel_radius 0.044 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m and the sensor layout at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m. Iterations 9 and 10 give the evidence.

If max_error rises above 0.069 on the slalom or s-bend, or noise_robustness is low, return wheel_radius to 0.04 m. Iteration 8 gave s-bend max_error 0.0684 at that value, which is inside the band. Do not return to mass 0.5 kg or wheel_track 0.14 m, since iterations 6 and 7 lowered progress.

Do not change sensor_size or the sensor span. Iterations 0 to 4 showed that span, footprint and lead changes leave max_error essentially unchanged, so further sensor work is unlikely to help the final track.
